title: Criminologists Licensure Examination (CLE)
disclaimer: Original practice items for educational simulation only. Not affiliated with PRC/CSC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: Under the Revised Penal Code, dolo refers to:
questions.explanation: Dolo = deliberate intent; culpa = fault/negligence.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: Justifying circumstances under the RPC generally:
choices: Exempt from criminal liability because the act is lawful
Are the same as aggravating circumstances
questions.explanation: Justifying circumstances make the act non-criminal.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: The national police force of the Philippines is the:
questions.explanation: Philippine National Police (PNP).

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: The primary purpose of police patrol is generally to:
choices: Prevent crime, protect life/property, and maintain order through presence and response
questions.explanation: Patrol is the backbone of police operations.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: First responders at a crime scene should prioritize:
choices: Safety, aid to victims, and scene preservation/security
Moving all evidence immediately without documentation
questions.explanation: Protect life, secure scene, preserve evidence.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: An interview is primarily:
choices: Accusatorial questioning of a suspect only
A non-accusatory conversation to gather information
questions.explanation: Interviews gather information.

questions.subject: Criminalistics
questions.stem: Fingerprints are valuable evidence primarily because they are:
questions.explanation: Friction ridge patterns are highly distinctive.

questions.subject: Criminalistics
questions.stem: Forensic ballistics generally studies:
questions.explanation: Ballistics covers arms and ammo-related evidence.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: The modern correctional philosophy emphasizes:
choices: Reformation/rehabilitation alongside safe custody and justice goals
questions.explanation: Corrections balances custody, justice, and rehabilitation.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: In the Philippines, city and municipal jails are generally under:
questions.explanation: BJMP handles city/municipal jails.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology and Ethics
questions.stem: Differential association theory mainly explains crime as learned through:
questions.explanation: Sutherland's differential association theory.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology and Ethics
questions.stem: A criminologist/law enforcer falsifying reports violates primarily:
choices: Professional ethics and possibly criminal law
questions.explanation: Integrity of reports is a core ethical and legal obligation.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: Principals by inducement are those who:
choices: Directly force or induce others to commit the crime
Are always accessories after the fact
questions.explanation: Principals include those who induce others to commit the crime.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: Community-oriented policing emphasizes:
choices: Partnership with the community to solve problems
questions.explanation: COP builds collaborative problem-solving.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: RA 10175 in the Philippines is known as the:
questions.explanation: RA 10175 is the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

questions.subject: Criminalistics
questions.stem: A questioned document examiner may analyze:
choices: Handwriting, signatures, and alterations on documents
questions.explanation: QD examination covers handwriting/signatures and alterations.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: Persons deprived of liberty retain rights that are:
choices: Limited by lawful confinement but not degraded of basic human dignity/rights
Identical to police powers of arrest
questions.explanation: PDL retain fundamental rights consistent with lawful custody.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology and Ethics
questions.stem: Victimology primarily studies:
choices: Victims of crime and victimization processes
questions.explanation: Victimology focuses on victims.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: Illegal drug cases in the Philippines are primarily governed by:
choices: RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act) and related issuances
questions.explanation: RA 9165 is the main special penal law on dangerous drugs.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: An effective police blotter/entry should be:
choices: Clear, factual, chronological, and properly identified
questions.explanation: Reports must be accurate, complete, and objective.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: Chain of custody primarily ensures:
choices: Evidence integrity and accountability from collection to presentation
questions.explanation: Chain of custody protects evidentiary integrity.

questions.subject: Criminalistics
questions.stem: Crime scene photographs should preferably be:
choices: Accurate, labeled, and taken before scene disturbance when possible
questions.explanation: Photos must accurately document the scene.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: Inmate classification helps institutions by:
choices: Matching custody/program needs to assessed risk and needs
questions.explanation: Classification supports safe and appropriate placement.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology and Ethics
questions.stem: During custodial investigation in the Philippines, the Bill of Rights primarily protects against:
choices: Forced confessions and denial of counsel, among other safeguards
questions.explanation: Constitutional rights in custodial investigation include counsel and protection vs coercion.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: Use of force by police should be:
choices: Lawful, necessary, and proportional to the threat
questions.explanation: Force must meet legality, necessity, and proportionality.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: Felonies are committed by means of deceit (dolo) or:
questions.explanation: Felonies are by dolo or culpa.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: A justifying circumstance generally means:
choices: The act is criminal and punished fully
The actor incurs no criminal liability
Only civil liability remains impossible always
questions.explanation: Justifying circumstances exempt from criminal liability.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: PNP is primarily under the administrative control/supervision framework linked to:
questions.explanation: PNP operates within DILG/NAPOLCOM structures.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: Visibility patrols mainly aim to:
choices: Deter crime and enhance public safety presence
questions.explanation: Patrol provides deterrence and service presence.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: The first officer’s priority at a scene is often to:
choices: Ensure safety and secure/preserve the scene
questions.explanation: Safety and scene security/preservation come first.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: Cognitive interviewing techniques emphasize:
choices: Facilitating accurate memory retrieval without contamination
questions.explanation: Cognitive interviews aid accurate recall.

questions.subject: Forensic Science
questions.stem: Fingerprint identification is valued because ridge patterns are:
questions.explanation: Fingerprints are highly individualized and persistent.

questions.subject: Forensic Science
questions.stem: Rifling marks on a bullet are useful for:
questions.explanation: Toolmarks/rifling support firearm ID.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: Rehabilitation as a correctional goal emphasizes:
questions.explanation: Rehabilitation aims at reform and reintegration.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: Classification of persons deprived of liberty helps:
questions.explanation: Classification supports safe and suitable placement/programs.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology
questions.stem: Strain theory associates crime with:
choices: Disjunction between cultural goals and legitimate means
questions.explanation: Strain highlights blocked legitimate means to valued goals.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology
questions.stem: Victimology studies:
questions.explanation: Victimology focuses on victims and victimization.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: Homicide under the RPC generally involves:
choices: Killing of a person without the qualifying circumstances of murder as defined
questions.explanation: Homicide is killing without murder’s qualifying circumstances.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: Problem-oriented policing focuses on:
choices: Identifying and addressing underlying crime problems
questions.explanation: POP analyzes and treats root crime problems.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: RA 10175 in the Philippines primarily addresses:
questions.explanation: RA 10175 is the Cybercrime Prevention Act.

questions.subject: Forensic Science
questions.stem: DNA evidence is powerful because it can:
choices: Link biological material to individuals with high discrimination
Date a crime to the exact minute alone always
questions.explanation: DNA can strongly associate biological evidence with persons.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: Probation generally allows a convicted person to:
choices: Serve sentence in community under supervision in lieu of imprisonment when granted
questions.explanation: Probation is community supervision as a sentencing alternative when legally available.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology
questions.stem: RA 9344 relates to:
questions.explanation: RA 9344 is the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: RA 9165 primarily concerns:
questions.explanation: RA 9165 is the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act.

questions.subject: Law Enforcement Administration
questions.stem: Crime analysis converting data into actionable insights is closest to:
questions.explanation: Analysis supports intelligence-led deployment.

questions.subject: Crime Detection and Investigation
questions.stem: A case folder should be:
choices: Posted publicly with all raw identities always
questions.explanation: Proper documentation preserves investigative integrity.

questions.subject: Forensic Science
questions.stem: Handwriting comparison can help determine:
questions.explanation: QD exams compare writing characteristics.

questions.subject: Correctional Administration
questions.stem: Persons deprived of liberty retain:
choices: Fundamental human rights subject to lawful limitations of custody
Voting rights in all foreign elections automatically
questions.explanation: Custody limits some liberties but core human rights remain.

questions.subject: Criminal Sociology
questions.stem: Situational crime prevention seeks to:
choices: Reduce opportunities for crime through environmental/design measures
questions.explanation: SCP reduces crime opportunities in immediate settings.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Jurisprudence
questions.stem: Corpus delicti refers to:
choices: The body/elements showing a crime was committed
questions.explanation: Corpus delicti is the substance of the crime committed.
